February 2I, 1970
Dear Debby:
I have been travelling so much in connection with aviation
and conservation activities that my mail has been terribly
neglected - letters stacked high and unopened -- five trips
around the world last year in addition to I don't know how
many to Europe and the west coast, etc. This is my second
trip to Europe within two weeks.
All in excuse for not writing
to you much sooner.
I don't keep a permanent secretary, and
temporary help is of little value to me in the kind of life I
I must be in Hawaii (Pan American) the first week of March.
Then, by the end of the week, in New York. Then the Philippines;
Japan; then Europe again. I'd like very much to help with
conservation activities on Captiva and Sanibel, but I don't see
how I can get to Florida in the near future. Anyway, I think
that to be effective the first steps must be taken by local
organization rather than anything I could do by flying down
there now. I suggest the following:
The Nature Conservancy is.

encountering on Captiva and Sanibel. The NC has assisted with
literally hundreds of conservation projects all over
the country,
and can give far better advice as to procedure than I can.
president is an extraordinarily able man, certainly one of the
best in the field.
(Last year, Anne gave a small island she
owned in Maine to the Nature Conservancy to include with its
Maine-coast-island project.)
I suggest that you write to Mr. Richards, the NC president,
for advice about procedures on Captiva and Sanibel. Don't
hesitate to say that I suggested this if you wish to. I expect
to see tir. Richards soon after I return to the United States,
and will also talk to him about it. I agree fully that it would
be a tragedy to have those wonderful islands spoiled through
excessive development.
Mr. Thomas W. Richards
President
Nature Conservancy
I522 K Street, N.W.
washington, D.C.
20005
Thanks a great deal lor the invitation to visit. Anne and
I would love to see you, and also to come to Captiva again. I
wish I could say we would hop on a plane and come right down; but
that is simply impossible for me at this time.
Best to you always, in which I know Anne joins me,
Chand
